This Appeal, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice N S Sanjay Gowda
 Oral Judgment
1.

The occurrence of the accident and the liability of the insurer to pay the compensation are also not in dispute.
2.
The claimant is in appeal.

3. As the doctor who treated the claimant was not examined, the Tribunal has only awarded sums towards 'pain and suffering', 'loss of amenities', NC: 2024:KHC:51171 'medical expenses' etc. in all amounting to Rs.2,45,111/-.
The claimant being aggrieved is in appeal.
4. In the absence of medical evidence stating any permanent disability having occurred to the claimant, the Tribunal was justified in not awarding any sums towards loss of future income.

However, it is noticed that the claimant had undergone a surgery and was hospitalized for 5 days, in my view, it would be appropriate to enhance the amounts awarded towards pain and suffering and loss of amenities from Rs.50,000/- to Rs.75,000/- each.

sentences.text:
It is also noticed that the accident of the year 2015 and the Tribunal has taken the notional income of Rs.7,000/- for granting compensation towards loss of income during the laid-up period,
since there was no proof of actual income.

As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority as determined the notional income of Rs.9,000/- for the accident of the year 2015, it NC:
2024:KHC:51171 would be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.9,000/-.
Consequently, towards 'loss of income during laid up period', the claimant would be entitled to Rs.27,000/- (Rs.9,000/- X 3 months) as against Rs.21,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

6. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,04,111/-
towards 'hospital and medical bills' and Rs.20,000/- towards 'food and nourishment charges'.
These sums are just and proper and are affirmed.

7. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:

9. The apportionment of liability shall be in the same terms as ordered by the Tribunal.
